title: introduce-kms-geotag-validator-and-rbacv2-assertion-multiplexer
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Customers with strict residency and audit requirements asked for stronger per-request proof that a chosen KMS key is region-eligible and that operator actions are permitted under RBACv2 policies. This PR implements a lightweight KMS geotag validator service + an RBACv2 assertion multiplexer that centralizes decision enrichment and reduces duplicate checks across gateways and the serving runtime.

What this changes: 1) cmd/kms-geotag-validator: new microservice that validates KMS key descriptors against residency rules and provider metadata; returns compact signed proofs (proof_v1) that are intended to be attached to audit events and cached by intermediate proxies. 2) pkg/auth/multiplexer: RBACv2 assertion multiplexer that aggregates policy inputs (service claims, tenant metadata, request zone) and emits canonical assertions consumed by runtime authorizers. 3) middleware/audit/enricher: attaches KMS proofs and assertion fingerprints into the sealed audit header to make later audits/verifications deterministic. 4) Integration glue in api-gateway to call the validator asynchronously and fall back to local heuristic when the validator is unreachable (configurable).

Design notes: - The KMS validator queries configured provider metadata stores (pluggable backends) and validates key tags, region claims, and issuer signatures. It then returns a signed minimal proof that includes: key_id, key_region, validator_id, timestamp, and a short HMAC (proof_v1). Proofs are valid for short TTLs (default 10m) to limit replay risk.
- The assertion multiplexer is intentionally deterministic: it normalizes inputs, orders attributes, and computes a stable fingerprint so RBAC decision caches across services can match the assertion. It supports incremental inputs so gateway -> runtime -> audit path can enrich the same assertion object rather than re-evaluating policies.
- Security: validator runs with least privilege to read provider metadata; it emits no secrets. All proofs are signed using the platform signing key and verified by authorizers using a public key rotation endpoint.

Implementation details: - cmd/kms-geotag-validator: Go binary with HTTP+gRPC endpoints. Lightweight LRU cache with singleflight dedupe for high QPS. Provider adapters for aws-kms, gcp-kms, and mock provider for tests. - pkg/auth/multiplexer: Go package with deterministic serializer and fingerprint function (sha256 over canonical JSON). - api-gateway: new non-blocking call path that attaches proof header X-RW-KMS-PROOF when available. - middleware/audit/enricher: extended sealed-audit header v2 to include kms_proof_fingerprint and assertion_fingerprint. Backwards-compatible with v1 storage.

Testing: unit tests for provider adapters (aws/gcp/mock), integration tests exercising gateway->validator->authorizer flow, and an end-to-end smoke run in benchmark-lab with a mock kms provider to assert audit envelopes contain the expected proof. Performance tests show the validator + LRU adds ~0.6ms p50 latency on a warm cache and handles deduped bursts of 1k TPS across a small cluster.

Migration and rollout: staged rollout using feature flags. Default behavior: validator disabled on clusters older than main-2025-10-01. A migration job will backfill proof fingerprints into recent audit indices for the last 48 hours to aid troubleshooting. The feature includes a safe fallback: when validator unreachable, gateway applies region heuristic (key tag region) and emits header X-RW-KMS-PROOF: heur/… with a warning flag to audit.

Checklist: - [x] API definition for proof_v1 and assertion fingerprinting - [x] Provider adapters (aws, gcp, mock) - [x] Gateway integration and non-blocking call path - [x] Audit middleware changes (backwards-compatible) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmark-lab scenario and perf baseline - [x] Docs: security/rbac/kms-geotag-validator.md

Related work: builds on earlier region/pinning efforts (see ENG-4321) and complements the residency attestor components. Not a replacement for long-term residency enforcement; provides per-request proof delegation for audit and decision caching.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the proof format, canonicalization of assertions, and the fallback strategy. I intentionally kept the validator stateless to simplify scaling; persistent caches are left to the platform cache tier if needed. For ops: the validator exposes telemetry (cache_hit_ratio, provider_errors, proof_sign_latency) and a /healthz readiness probe.

Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-6152/kms-geotag-validator-design, benchmark scenario https://bench.example.internal/runs/2025-11-04/validator-smoke

Gateway integration and middleware audit envelope enrichment
Add unit tests and benchmark-lab scenario
Fix linter & boundary case for missing key tags
review_comments: Aaron Chen: Please clarify the TTL rationale for proof_v1; short TTL helps reduce replay risk but increases calls — can we make TTL configurable per cluster?
Sofia Martinez: replied: TTL is configurable via feature flag and cluster config; default 10m is conservative. Added CLI flag and env var.
Priya Desai: Request to add an explicit verification path in the authorizer to fail closed for proofs with missing validator signature.

Sofia Martinez: replied: added signature verification step in pkg/auth/authorizer and unit tests; authorizer will now return 403 if proof signature missing/invalid unless the cluster is in 'heuristic-allow' mode (ops-only).
Liam O'Connor: Noted linter failures on golangci — requested style fixes in multiplexer canonicalization
Sofia Martinez: replied: addressed style and added comments and additional test cases
ci_summary: First CI run: golangci/fail (fixed), unit-tests/pass, integration/pending. Second CI run: all checks pass. Benchmarks executed in benchmark-lab and attached as artifacts.
release_notes: Add KMS geotag validator service (proof_v1) and RBACv2 assertion multiplexer. Enables per-request signed KMS residency proofs and normalized assertion fingerprints for consistent authorization and audit. Backwards-compatible audit header v2; safe fallback to heuristic when validator unavailable.
